patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.quote: I've lost count - at least a dozen watery trips a day. I was only in the hospital three nights for that leg infection, and the diarrhea started a few days after I finished their antibiotics.
presentation.triageNote: 70-year-old male with four days of frequent profuse watery diarrhea and abdominal cramping shortly after a hospital admission and a course of clindamycin, now weak and clinically dehydrated without bloody stool.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player's assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 3 is appropriate because older age, profuse diarrhea, fever, tachycardia, borderline blood pressure, and dehydration require multiple infectious and treatment resources.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This recently hospitalized patient has antibiotic-associated profuse watery diarrhea with dehydration and possible infectious colitis.
clinical.acuityReason: Older age, profuse diarrhea, fever, tachycardia, borderline blood pressure, and dehydration require multiple infectious and treatment resources.
expectedResources: CBC, metabolic, lactate, and stool testing
keyFindings: Four days of profuse watery diarrhea
teachingPoints: Older age, recent healthcare exposure, clindamycin and new profuse watery diarrhea are the classic cluster for C. diff. Do not wait for the stool result to protect everyone else: isolate on suspicion, use soap-and-water hand hygiene and assess dehydration and colitis severity.
Triage should be based on the current presentation and expected care, with reassessment if new warning signs appear.

possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: Isolation, testing, and IV rehydration would guide admission based on colitis severity and treatment response.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.

Match the attached reference image's painterly style. Full-body wide shot, square 1:1, 3/4 front view, centered. Show the entire person and entire blue padded clinic chair with all feet and chair legs and generous margin. Subject: a white 70-year-old man in a loose polo shirt and casual trousers. Pose: leaning forward slightly, one forearm across his lower abdomen, the other hand holding a clear water bottle. Expression: drained, uncomfortable and exhausted. Visible signs: dry lips, tired eyes, slightly sunken cheeks; no stool, toilet, vomiting or graphic content. No text, logos, medical equipment, shadows, floor plane, watermark or border.
